Subject: ACME POC integration plan & success criteria

Hi Alex / Priya 

Great to meet earlier today. Quick recap + proposed POC plan so we're all aligned: 

Success criteria (what Acme will measure):
- Basic feature parity: Redwood can replicate current generation quality for helpdesk replies (F1/quality target: >= 92% per your eval prompt set).
- Latency: median generation p50 < 350ms for 256-token prompts under your test load (see load profile in attached sheet).
- Cost envelope: per-conversation token cost within the threshold you shared (~$0.002/token).
- Tool-calling: Redwood function-calling can successfully invoke your internal KB tool in our test scenario (round-trip < 500ms).

Proposed evaluation plan / timeline:
- Week 0 (this week): NDA/procurement paperwork + provide access details for the test environment.
- Week 1 (integration): SDK install, API key exchange, basic generation & embeddings integration.
- Week 2 (validation): latency/cost profiling, streaming & tool-calling tests, collect metrics.
- Week 3 (results): review, iterate, hand-off to procurement for next steps.

Ownership:
- Redwood: Marissa (commercial lead), Dev Patel (technical lead).
- Acme: Priya (engineering lead), Alex (PM / product owner).

Tech notes / asks for kickoff:
- We'll provide an SDK and a compact integration guide (attached) with code samples for streaming and function-calling.
- Please share a dev API host / sandbox IP whitelist + a short list of evaluation prompts.
- Any compliance constraints (retention, IP, SOC2 evidence)  flag here so we can loop security.

Attachments: acme_poc_success_criteria.xlsx

Next steps: Please confirm success criteria above and availability for a 30-minute technical kickoff next week.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Hi Alex / Priya 

Quick tech note and sample endpoints to help your engineers plan. Attaching a compact SDK guide (redwood_sdk_integration_guide.pdf) with code snippets. Highlights below: 

1) SDK and auth
- SDKs: JavaScript (node), Python, and a curl reference. Install via npm / pip.
- Auth: API key with scoped roles; for sandbox we'll provision a time-limited key.

2) Core endpoints (examples)- Text generation: POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate payload: {"model":"rwd-1.0","input":"..."}
- Chat / structured: POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat  supports messages array and system/user roles.
- Embeddings: POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings

3) Streaming / realtime- Streaming is available via Server-Sent Events (GET https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams?session=*) and WebSocket client for lower-latency token events.
- We support chunked token callbacks, partial-offers, and reconnect semantics.

4) Tool-calling / function calling- Redwood uses JSON-schema for function definitions in the request; model will return a structured call object when applicable. Example: include "functions": [{"name":"kb_lookup","schema":{...}}] in request.
- The SDK exposes a helper to automatically call your tool endpoint and pass arguments; we can also hand control to your service to validate and return results.

5) Performance knobs (for POC)
- Batching: disable (single-request) vs enable small batching for throughput tests.
- KV cache: prefix caching supported; useful for conversational state.
- Quantization: we can propose a quantized variant for cost testing if you want lower cost but slightly different perf characteristics.

6) Observability / logs
- Token-level latency/cost metrics available in the Redwood Console.
- For PII concerns: we offer an option to disable long-term logs for a namespace and an export pipeline for audit. I'll pull the security summary doc and send separately.

Proposed tech kickoff: Thu 2026-03-18 16:00 ET (30 min)  I can join and walk through integration snippets and run a live tool-calling test if you provide a test endpoint.

Attachments: redwood_sdk_integration_guide.pdf
